title: Caching Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit cache policy, provider capabilities, channels, and verification.
owner: Nodics cache contracts and configured provider
summary: Every channel must declare source authority, key scope, eligibility, TTL, invalidation, provider requirements, fallback, diagnostics, and tests.

sections.heading: Authority and selection
items: nCache provides the provider-neutral contract and resolves the configured adapter; NodeCache, Redis, and qualified Hazelcast support different topology and operational needs.
Callers never import provider SDKs or treat a cache entry as business authority. The owning database/service contract can rebuild cached projections.
Only the configured provider path is active for a cache role. Fallback behavior is explicit and must not create two writable cache authorities.

sections.heading: Keys, values, and lifetime
items: A key includes tenant and every context dimension that changes the result, uses stable bounded encoding, and never contains credentials or sensitive raw identifiers.
Values are safe serializable projections with schema/version identity where compatibility requires it; mutable business objects are not shared by reference.
TTL, maximum size, eviction, null caching, stale policy, and namespace are configured according to data volatility and failure tolerance.

sections.heading: Read and invalidation lifecycle
items: Read-through checks cache, loads from the owning service on miss, and stores only a successful safe projection. Stampede protection bounds concurrent loaders.

Successful authoritative mutations invalidate or replace only affected keys after persistence. Publication, price, stock, context, permission, and relationship changes include their dependent dimensions.
Broad flush is an operational recovery tool, not the normal consistency design; invalidation is idempotent and observable.

sections.heading: Provider behavior and outages
items: NodeCache is process-local and cannot provide shared distributed session or authorization atomicity. Redis supports qualified shared operations; Hazelcast requires its own compatibility evidence.
Failure policy may bypass cache and load authority for safe reads, fail closed for security/session state, or reject work under overload according to the caller contract.
Circuit, timeout, retry, serialization, connection, and shutdown behavior are normalized without hiding provider-specific operational requirements.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test hit, miss, expiry, eviction, invalidation, stampede, negative caching, serialization, version mismatch, tenant isolation, outage, recovery, and provider switching.
Run multi-node atomicity, failover, load, memory, connection, rolling restart, security, TLS, secret rotation, backup assumptions, and supported-version qualification where applicable.
Monitor hit ratio, latency, errors, bypass, evictions, loader duration, invalidation lag, key volume, memory, circuit state, and saturation with bounded labels.

sections.heading: Provider capability checklist
items: Distribution and consistency scope.
TTL and non-expiring support.
Atomic consume and conditional operations.
Single-key and prefix invalidation.
Serialization and maximum key/value limits.
Diagnostics, readiness, reconnect, and close.

sections.heading: Channel checklist
items: Owner and authoritative fallback.
Tenant, enterprise, catalog, principal, locale, and permission key partitions.
Cacheability and negative-result policy.
TTL, acceptable staleness, and invalidation event.
Outage bypass versus fail-closed behavior.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, multi-node integration, performance, security, and regression tests.
